data.title: Show HN: I wrote a BitTorrent Client from scratch
data.author: piyushgupta53
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个用Go语言实现的BitTorrent客户端——go-torrent-client。该项目实现了BitTorrent客户端的核心功能，包括种子文件解析、节点发现与通信以及文件下载。主要特性包括Bencode编码/解码、种子文件处理、节点发现与通信、以及下载管理（如分片和块管理、进度跟踪等）。项目结构清晰，包含命令行界面、内部包（如Bencode编码、种子处理、节点协议等）以及公共包。目前该项目正在积极开发中，未来计划支持磁力链接、元数据交换协议和DHT。需要Go 1.21或更高版本进行安装和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言实现的BitTorrent客户端的实现细节、安全性、功能完整性及潜在改进方向

不同观点：
• [jorkingit] 认为需要限制bencode解码器中的动态分配大小，以防止恶意输入通过请求极大的分配来导致拒绝服务（DoS）攻击。建议将剩余的输入长度作为上限。
• [vkaku] 对项目表示赞赏，并建议在README中添加简单的使用说明，例如如何通过命令行下载.torrent文件。此外，还建议添加从URL解析torrent文件的功能。
• [__jonas] 提到一个名为codecrafters的平台，该平台提供相关课程并包含测试，可以作为实现BitTorrent客户端的指导。
• [ashirviskas] 作为一个非Go开发者，询问为什么使用较旧的Go版本1.21，并指出该版本已在10个月前被弃用。
• [agiron123] 表示该项目让他们回想起大学时的网络课程项目，并认为这种项目是学习新语言的好方法。
• [vivzkestrel] 对项目的构建过程表示好奇，询问作者是参考了协议文档还是通过其他实现来构建项目。

补充讨论：
• [NooneAtAll3] 询问是否支持磁力链接，并在编辑中提到这似乎是一个计划中的功能。
• [TheEdonian] 询问为该项目添加图形用户界面（GUI）的难度，并表示对Go语言的GUI实现不熟悉。
• [throwaway894345] 对项目的完整性和处理复杂功能（如DHT、磁力链接、NAT traversal）的能力表示关注，并询问项目的完成度和实现难度。
• [NoMoreNicksLeft] 询问是否实现了v2和可变torrent，并表示对可变torrent的支持非常重要。
• [OccamsMirror] 询问该项目是否可以作为库使用。
• [b0a04gl] 认为项目在崩溃恢复、加密握手、uTP支持和NAT行为等方面缺乏说明，并指出在真实环境中可能存在风险。建议增加模块化设计和内存保护机制，并提到需要一个roadmap。

争议焦点：
• 项目的安全性和功能完整性是主要争议点。一些评论者关注项目在处理恶意输入、复杂BitTorrent功能（如DHT、磁力链接）、以及在真实环境中的稳定性方面的能力。
• 另外，使用较旧的Go版本也引起了一些讨论。

Go-Torrent
A BitTorrent client implementation in Go that supports downloading files using the BitTorrent protocol. This project implements the core functionality of a BitTorrent client, including torrent file parsing, peer discovery, and file downloading.
Features
Bencode Encoding/Decoding
Support for all Bencode types (strings, integers, lists, dictionaries)
Robust error handling and validation
Torrent File Processing
Parse .torrent files (both single-file and multi-file torrents)
Info hash calculation
Piece hash extraction
Support for all standard torrent file fields
Peer Discovery and Communication
HTTP tracker support
Peer handshake protocol
Complete BitTorrent message protocol
Peer connection management
Download Functionality
Piece and block management
Concurrent downloads
Progress tracking
File assembly for both single and multi-file torrents
Storage management with block-level granularity
Project Structure
.
├── cmd/          # Command-line interface and main application
├── internal/     # Internal packages
│   ├── bencode/  # Bencode encoding/decoding
│   ├── torrent/  # Torrent file processing
│   ├── tracker/  # Tracker protocol implementation
│   ├── peer/     # Peer communication
│   └── download/ # Download management
└── pkg/          # Public packages
Requirements
Go 1.21 or later
Installation
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/go-torrent.git
cd
go-torrent
go mod download
Usage
[Usage instructions will be added as the project matures]
Development Status
This project is actively under development. Current implementation status can be found in
checkpoint.md
.
Planned Features
Magnet link support
Metadata exchange protocol
DHT (Distributed Hash Table) support

data.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
data.author: archon1410
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为SEAL（Self-Adapting Language Models）的框架，使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过生成自己的微调数据和更新指令进行自我适应。SEAL模型在接收到新输入时，会生成自编辑内容，这些内容可以重构信息、指定优化超参数或调用工具进行数据增强和基于梯度的更新。通过监督微调（SFT），这些自编辑会导致持久的权重更新，实现持续适应。为了训练模型生成有效的自编辑，文章使用了一个以更新后模型的下游性能作为奖励信号的强化学习循环。实验表明，SEAL在知识整合和少样本泛化方面表现出色，是语言模型自我导向适应的有前景的一步。相关代码和网站已提供。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）的自适应学习能力及其实用性

不同观点：
• **perrygeo**：LLMs缺乏像人类一样的持续学习能力，它们的训练和推理过程是分离的。这种静态特性导致人们误以为AGI（通用人工智能）即将到来，但实际上LLMs在推理结束后就停止了学习。
• **gavinray**：提到NEAT/HyperNEAT算法，这种算法通过演化网络拓扑来优化学习，与LLMs通过调整权重来学习的做法形成对比。他的两位从事ML早期的朋友坚信强化学习（RL）和演化算法是ML的未来方向。
• **xianshou**：赞赏自我编辑方法通过RL优化模型重构信息的能力，指出该方法可以发现更好的训练格式，但仍存在灾难性遗忘问题和高计算开销。他认为该方法适用于高价值文档处理，但限制于需要明确评估指标的任务。
• **libraryofbabel**：对LLMs在实际应用中“边做边学”的能力表示关注，质疑为何当前研究不更多关注这一方向，并指出这可能是实现AGI的关键障碍。

补充讨论：
• **cma**：提到Anthropic最近关于自我微调的研究，提供了一个相关的文献链接。
• **neuroelectron**：幽默地提到模型在实际应用中被限制为只读模式，类似于科幻电影中的情节。
• **all2**：提供了一个包含代码和示例的网站链接。
• **khalic**：引用研究预测到2028年LLMs将用尽所有公开的文本数据，指出合成数据增强的重要性，并建议通过元训练一个专门的SEAL合成数据生成器模型来解决数据墙问题。
• **Centigonal**：提出“正确遗忘”问题比“正确学习”问题更迫切，指出当前模型在遗忘不相关信息方面的能力不足。
• **b0a04gl**：质疑自我编辑模型的调试难度，担心如何确定错误输出是源于基础模型还是模型的自我编辑，并进一步讨论优化器行为监控的必要性。
• **yahoozoo**：质疑SEAL方法的创新性，认为其仅是利用HuggingFace库进行LoRA适配器的合并。
• **mackenziebowes**：对SEAL命名表示不满，认为SAL更为合适。
• **bravesoul2**：简单提到正接近重大突破。
• **ivape**：指出持续微调在云端LLMs上的可行性问题，认为当前硬件条件尚不支持这一设想。

争议焦点：
• LLMs的持续学习能力及其实际应用的可行性。
• 自我编辑方法的创新性和实用性。
• 调试和监控自我学习模型的难度。
• 数据墙问题及合成数据增强的潜在解决方案。

Title:
Self-Adapting Language Models
Authors:
Adam Zweiger
,
Jyothish Pari
,
Han Guo
,
Ekin Akyürek
,
Yoon Kim
,
Pulkit Agrawal
View a PDF of the paper titled Self-Adapting Language Models, by Adam Zweiger and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are powerful but static; they lack mechanisms to adapt their weights in response to new tasks, knowledge, or examples. We introduce Self-Adapting LLMs (SEAL), a framework that enables LLMs to self-adapt by generating their own finetuning data and update directives. Given a new input, the model produces a self-edit-a generation that may restructure the information in different ways, specify optimization hyperparameters, or invoke tools for data augmentation and gradient-based updates. Through supervised finetuning (SFT), these self-edits result in persistent weight updates, enabling lasting adaptation. To train the model to produce effective self-edits, we use a reinforcement learning loop with the downstream performance of the updated model as the reward signal. Unlike prior approaches that rely on separate adaptation modules or auxiliary networks, SEAL directly uses the model's own generation to control its adaptation process. Experiments on knowledge incorporation and few-shot generalization show that SEAL is a promising step toward language models capable of self-directed adaptation. Our website and code is available at

data.title: MUMPS
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
MUMPS（Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System），又称M，是一种无类型、面向过程的编程语言，具有集成的事务处理键-值数据库。它由Neil Pappalardo、Robert A. Greenes和Curt Marble于1966-1967年在波士顿麻省总医院（MGH）开发，最初用于管理病人医疗记录和医院实验室信息系统。MUMPS后来成为美国健康信息系统和电子健康记录的主流数据库技术，如Epic Systems使用MUMPS为超过78%的美国患者提供服务。

MUMPS起源于对使用汇编语言开发医院信息系统的不满，其设计目标包括跨平台可移植性和多任务处理。该语言早期在PDP-7和PDP-9上运行，后来移植到多种系统如PDP-8、PDP-11等。MUMPS因其独特的集成数据库语言和高效的磁盘读写能力而广受医疗界欢迎。
data.comments_summary:

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Programming language
This article is about the programming language. For the disease, see
Mumps
. For other uses, see
Mumps (disambiguation)
.
MUMPS
Paradigm
Imperative
,
procedural
Designed by
Neil Pappalardo
,  Curt Marble,
Robert A. Greenes
First appeared
1966
; 59 years ago
(
1966
)
Stable release
ANSI X11.1-1995
/    December 8, 1995
(
1995-12-08
)
Typing discipline
Typeless

Cross-platform
Influenced by
JOSS
Influenced
PSL
,
Caché ObjectScript
,
GT.M
MUMPS
("Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System"), or
M
, is an imperative, high-level
programming language
with an integrated transaction processing
key–value database
.  It was originally developed at
Massachusetts General Hospital
for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
MUMPS technology has since expanded as the predominant database for health information systems and
electronic health records
in the United States.  MUMPS-based information systems, such as
Epic Systems
', provide health information services for over 78% of patients across the U.S.
[
1
]
A unique feature of the MUMPS technology is its integrated
database language
, allowing direct, high-speed read-write access to permanent disk storage.
[
2
]
History
[
edit
]
1960s-1970s - Genesis
[
edit
]
MUMPS was developed by
Neil Pappalardo
,
Robert A. Greenes
, and Curt Marble in Dr. Octo Barnett's lab at the
Massachusetts General Hospital
(MGH) in
Boston
during 1966 and 1967.
[
3
]
It grew out of frustration, during a
National Institutes of Health
(NIH) supported hospital information systems project at the MGH, with the development in assembly language on a time-shared
PDP-1
by primary contractor
Bolt, Beranek & Newman
(BBN).  MUMPS came out of an internal "
skunkworks
" project at MGH by Pappalardo, Greenes, and Marble to create an alternative development environment. As a result of initial demonstration of capabilities, Dr. Barnett's proposal to NIH in 1967 for renewal of the hospital computer project grant took the bold step of proposing that the system be built in MUMPS going forward, rather than relying on the BBN approach. The project was funded, and serious implementation of the system in MUMPS began.
The original MUMPS system was, like
Unix
a few years later, built on a
DEC
PDP-7
. Octo Barnett and Neil Pappalardo obtained a
backward compatible
PDP-9
, and began using MUMPS in the admissions cycle and laboratory test reporting. MUMPS was then an
interpreted language
, yet even then, it incorporated a
hierarchical database
file system to standardize interaction with the data and abstract disk operations so they were only done by the MUMPS language itself. MUMPS was also used in its earliest days in an experimental clinical progress note entry system
[
4
]
and a radiology report entry system.
[
5
]
Some aspects of MUMPS can be traced from
RAND Corporation
's
JOSS
through
BBN
's
TELCOMP
and
STRINGCOMP
.  The MUMPS team chose to include portability between machines as a design goal.
An advanced feature of the MUMPS language not widely supported in
operating systems
or in
computer hardware
of the era was
multitasking
. Although
time-sharing
on
mainframe computers
was increasingly common in systems such as
Multics
, most mini-computers did not run parallel programs and threading was not available at all. Even on mainframes, the variant of batch processing where a program was run to completion was the most common implementation for an operating system of multi-programming.
It was a few years until Unix was developed. The lack of memory management hardware also meant that all multi-processing was fraught with the possibility that a memory pointer could change some other process. MUMPS programs do not have a standard way to refer to memory directly at all, in contrast to
C language
, so since the multitasking was enforced by the language, not by any program written in the language it was impossible to have the risk that existed for other systems.
Dan Brevik's DEC MUMPS-15 system was adapted to a DEC
PDP-15
, where it lived for some time. It was first installed at Health Data Management Systems of Denver in May 1971.
[
6
]
The portability proved to be useful and MUMPS was awarded a government research grant, and so MUMPS was released to the public domain which was a requirement for grants. MUMPS was soon ported to a number of other systems including the popular DEC
PDP-8
, the
Data General Nova
and on DEC
PDP-11
and the
Artronix
PC12 minicomputer
. Word about MUMPS spread mostly through the medical community, and was in widespread use, often being locally modified for their own needs.
Versions of the MUMPS system were rewritten by technical leaders Dennis "Dan" Brevik and Paul Stylos
[
6
]
of
DEC
in 1970 and 1971. By the early 1970s, there were many and varied implementations of MUMPS on a range of hardware platforms. Another noteworthy platform was Paul Stylos'
[
6
]
DEC MUMPS-11 on the PDP-11,
44272140.article_summary:
MUMPS（Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System），又称M，是一种无类型、面向过程的编程语言，具有集成的事务处理键-值数据库。它由Neil Pappalardo、Robert A. Greenes和Curt Marble于1966-1967年在波士顿麻省总医院（MGH）开发，最初用于管理病人医疗记录和医院实验室信息系统。MUMPS后来成为美国健康信息系统和电子健康记录的主流数据库技术，如Epic Systems使用MUMPS为超过78%的美国患者提供服务。

MUMPS起源于对使用汇编语言开发医院信息系统的不满，其设计目标包括跨平台可移植性和多任务处理。该语言早期在PDP-7和PDP-9上运行，后来移植到多种系统如PDP-8、PDP-11等。MUMPS因其独特的集成数据库语言和高效的磁盘读写能力而广受医疗界欢迎。

data.title: Thiings
data.author: pentagrama
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了如何在找不到所需物品时进行操作。如果用户在收藏中找不到特定物品，可以申请请求该物品。文章提供了一个链接，用户可以通过点击"Request a Thiing"来提交他们的请求。这一功能方便用户获取未包含在当前收藏中的所需物品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Thiings网站及其内容、功能、版权和实用性的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• [paxys] 质疑网站声称的"免费"性质，因为下载整个图标集合需要付费。同时，对内容许可协议表示困惑，指出网站声称任何人都可以下载和使用图标，但未明确说明具体的许可类型。
• [huhtenberg] 提到另一个类似的但更全面的网站——The Noun Project，暗示Thiings的独特性和实用性可能不如竞争对手。
• [dvh] 对网站的搜索功能提出批评，指出搜索结果不准确，例如搜索“asp”时没有相关选项，却出现了“wasp”。
• [timnetworks] 指出网站在音频播放方面存在加载时间问题，导致音频播放时可能不完整。
• [fredley] 指出网站上伦敦桥的图片有误，实际展示的是塔桥，反映了内容准确性的问题。
• [toddmorey] 对如何生成具有风格一致性的自定义图标表示兴趣，寻求资源和建议。
• [wvbdmp] 对网站包含军事内容如“Reaper Drone”和“坦克”，但没有某些日常生活物品如“dildo”表示不解。

补充讨论：
• [_august] 提供了一个相关的GitHub项目链接，用于生成Genmoji风格的图像，扩展了讨论的范围。
• [awfulneutral] 对网站上恐龙图像的科学准确性提出批评，特别是与《侏罗纪公园》相关的图像。
• [Waterluvian] 认为网站在手机上的导航体验不佳，但认为其设计接近令人愉快，提出了改进建议。
• [HanClinto] 对网站的存在目的和持续性表示怀疑，并对网站的版权语言和商业模式提出疑问，指出其未使用明确的CC-BY-NC等许可协议。
• [the-anarchist] 对如何保存图案和调整背景颜色提出技术性问题，寻求解决方案。
• [Centigonal] 认为网站的商业模式难以在市场竞争中长期生存，指出图标市场竞争激烈且成本低。
• [kurrupttt] 对网站的内容表示满意，认为其提供的3D元素对个人项目非常有用，持积极态度。
• [ipsum2] 认为网站的AI生成图标质量较高，但没有明确的使用场景。

争议焦点：
• 网站内容的免费与付费下载之间的矛盾以及内容许可的不明确性是主要的争议点。
• 网站内容的科学准确性和搜索功能的准确性也引发了用户的批评。
• 网站的商业模式和长期生存能力受到质疑。

总结：用户对Thiings网站的图标质量和创意表示了一定的认可，但在内容许可、功能实现和商业模式等方面提出了较多质疑和改进建议。

data.title: Student discovers fungus predicted by Albert Hoffman
data.author: zafka
data.article_summary: 西弗吉尼亚大学（WVU）环境微生物学专业的学生Corinne Hazel发现了一种新的真菌物种，这种真菌可能用于治疗多种医疗疾病。她在研究牵牛花如何通过根部分泌麦角生物碱时，发现了一种名为*Periglandula clandestina*的新真菌，这种真菌能够产生与LSD类似的效果。她的发现是在与植物与土壤科学教授Daniel Panaccione合作下完成的，并得到了WVU Davis学院学生增强基金的资助。基因测序确认了这一新物种，其基因序列现已存入基因库。这种真菌能高效生产麦角生物碱，可能在未来药物开发中发挥重要作用。Hazel目前正在研究如何最佳地培养这种生长缓慢的真菌，并探索其他牵牛花物种是否也含有未被描述的真菌共生体。这一发现为医药和农业研究开辟了新的方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：与LSD、麦角生物碱、植物与真菌共生关系相关的科学发现及其影响

不同观点：
• [driggs] 认为霍夫曼（Albert Hoffman）在研究麦角酸酰二乙氨（LSA）时被指责样本污染，但后来由于植物与内共生真菌的关系被澄清而得到平反。霍夫曼的早期工作未考虑到植物内的隐秘真菌，但他的发现最终被证明是正确的。
• [Zaylan] 对新发现的共生关系表示赞赏，并推测自然界中可能还有许多未被发现的隐藏“化学家”——即在植物中悄悄进行复杂代谢过程的真菌。这引发了对日常植物中潜在未开发潜力的思考。
• [hollerith] 引用YouTube视频内容，质疑LSD可能引发创伤后应激障碍（PTSD），并提供视频链接以支持其观点，尽管未提供具体时间索引。
• [doormatt] 对研究中基因组测序的“重要性”提出质疑，认为既然测序是由外部公司完成的，那么其意义是否如文章所述那样重大。
• [homeonthemtn] 赞赏文章对迷幻化合物讨论时采取的成熟 tone（语气），表明对讨论此类敏感话题时应持谨慎态度。
• [gwbas1c] 对LSD被用于治疗抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍和成瘾等疾病的说法表示困惑，指出LSD属于附表1药物，理论上不应有合法用途，并提到与MDMA的合法实验情况不同。
• [randomNumber7] 强调LSA与LSD的不同，指出LSA可以从法律上获得，但其危险性可能高于LSD。
• [throwing_away] 询问是否可以获取克隆用于研究目的，显示出对研究资源的关注。
• [scythe] 指出，虽然麦角生物碱的合成衍生物（如麦角新碱）常用于治疗偏头痛、痴呆等疾病，但天然麦角本身难以培养，因此发现新的共生真菌具有重要意义。
• [zer00eyz] 对文章中LSD被用于治疗多种疾病的描述表示怀疑，认为这句话反映出文章在LSD问题上的语气存在问题，暗示LSD仍然是一个有争议的物质。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是LSD是否可以合法用于治疗目的，以及文章对LSD的描述是否准确。部分评论者对LSD的合法性和安全性提出质疑。
• 另一讨论点是基因组测序的“重要性”问题，尤其是当测序工作外包给其他公司时，其科学价值是否如文章所述那样重大。
• 评论中还涉及LSA与LSD的区别，以及LSA的合法性和潜在危险性。

44243059.article_content:
WVU student discovers long-awaited mystery fungus sought by LSD’s inventor
Monday, June 02, 2025
Corinne Hazel, a WVU environmental microbiology major from Delaware, Ohio, has discovered a new species of fungus that may treat a variety of medical conditions.
(WVU Photo/Brian Persinger)
Download full-size
Making a discovery with the
potential for innovative applications in pharmaceutical development, a
West Virginia University
microbiology
student has found a long sought-after fungus that produces effects similar to the
semisynthetic drug LSD, which is used to treat conditions like depression,
post-traumatic stress disorder and addiction.
Corinne Hazel, of Delaware,
Ohio, an environmental microbiology major and
Goldwater
Scholar
, discovered the new species of fungus growing in morning
glory plants and named it Periglandula clandestina.
Hazel made the discovery
while working in the lab with
Daniel
Panaccione
, Davis-Michael Professor
of
Plant
and Soil Sciences
at the
WVU Davis College of Agriculture and
Natural Resources
. She
was studying how morning glories disperse protective chemicals called “ergot
alkaloids” through their roots when she saw evidence of a fungus.
“We had a ton of plants
lying around and they had these tiny little seed coats,” she said. “We noticed a
little bit of fuzz in the seed coat. That was our fungus.”
The researchers prepared a DNA sample
and sent it away for genome sequencing, funded by a
WVU Davis
College Student Enhancement Grant
obtained by Hazel. The sequencing confirmed
the discovery of a new species and the sequence is now deposited in a gene bank
with her name on it.
“Sequencing a genome is a significant
thing,” Panaccione said. “It’s amazing for a student.”
Morning glory plants live
in symbiosis with fungi that produce the same ergot alkaloids the Swiss chemist
Albert Hofmann modified when he invented LSD in the late 1930s.
Hofmann hypothesized that
a fungus in morning glories produced alkaloids similar to those in LSD, but the
species remained a mystery until Hazel and Panaccione’s discovery. They published their findings in
Mycologia
.
“Morning glories contain
high concentrations of similar lysergic acid derivatives that give them their
psychedelic activities,” Panaccione said. “This inspired Hofmann and others to
investigate morning glories for the presence of a hidden fungus related to the
ergot fungus that might be the source of these chemicals. They found very
similar chemicals, but they could never find the fungus itself.”
Ergot alkaloids are made
exclusively by fungi. In addition to morning glories, they’re often found
growing on grains like rye. They can be poisonous to humans and livestock and, when
used therapeutically, can have unwanted side effects. Still, some clinicians use
them to treat conditions like migraines, dementia, uterine hemorrhaging and
Parkinson’s disease.
Periglandula clandestina is highly
efficient at making ergot alkaloids in large quantities, a characteristic that may
play a role in future pharmaceuticals. The discovery of the fungus o
pens a host of potential research
avenues, Panaccione said.
“Many things are toxic. But if you
administer them in the right dosage or modify them, they can be useful
pharmaceuticals. By studying them, we may be able to figure out ways to bypass
the side effects. These are big issues for medicine and agriculture.”
The researchers dubbed the fungus “Periglandula
clandestina” for its ability to have eluded investigators for decades.
“I think that’s the perfect name,”
Panaccione said. “And I love that we did this project together. Corinne has a
ton of talent. It’s about students recognizing the opportunities, seizing them
and having the skill and the brain power to bring this work to fruition.”
Hazel is now studying the most
effective ways to culture the slow-growing fungus and is interested in whether other
morning glory species may also contain ergot alkaloids from a fungal symbiote
that has yet to be described.
“I’m lucky to have stumbled into this
opportunity,” she said. “People have been looking for this fungus for years,
and one day, I look in the right place, and there it is. I’m very proud of the
work that I’ve done at WVU.”
-WVU-

44243059.article_summary: 西弗吉尼亚大学（WVU）环境微生物学专业的学生Corinne Hazel发现了一种新的真菌物种，这种真菌可能用于治疗多种医疗疾病。她在研究牵牛花如何通过根部分泌麦角生物碱时，发现了一种名为*Periglandula clandestina*的新真菌，这种真菌能够产生与LSD类似的效果。她的发现是在与植物与土壤科学教授Daniel Panaccione合作下完成的，并得到了WVU Davis学院学生增强基金的资助。基因测序确认了这一新物种，其基因序列现已存入基因库。这种真菌能高效生产麦角生物碱，可能在未来药物开发中发挥重要作用。Hazel目前正在研究如何最佳地培养这种生长缓慢的真菌，并探索其他牵牛花物种是否也含有未被描述的真菌共生体。这一发现为医药和农业研究开辟了新的方向。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为Bloxi的项目，它是一个由帝国理工学院航空工程二年级学生开发的AI助手，能够将自然语言提示转换为可运行的Simulink控制系统模型，并进行实时调试。该项目利用OpenAI的API实现多模态功能，可以逐步生成和连接Simulink模块，并通过截图和LLM检查不一致之处。项目包含两个主要脚本和一个简单后端，用户只需输入自己的OpenAI API密钥即可使用。尽管最初只是个人项目，但随着MathWorks宣布开发类似工具，作者决定分享Bloxi，以供他人进一步开发和使用。项目遵循MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Matlab和Simulink的应用及其工具的优缺点

不同观点：
• [kaamuli] 认为Matlab和Simulink在实际操作中存在效率问题，尤其是在构建和调试控制系统模型时，手动连接模块会浪费大量时间。为此，他开发了Bloxi，一个基于AI的助手，能够将自然语言提示转换为Simulink模型，并实时调试。他强调Bloxi的开发初衷是为了提高生产力，并分享了自己的开发经验和代码，希望其他人能进一步改进。

• [stochtastic] 则指出，虽然Matlab和Simulink在某些行业和学术领域已经不再流行，但它们在某些特定领域仍然具有无可比拟的优势。他提到对MathWorks产品的负面评价主要集中在许可证和商业模式上，而忽视了其技术优势。他鼓励不要被负面评价影响，认为应根据具体任务选择合适的工具。

补充讨论：
• [kaamuli] 提到了开发Bloxi过程中解决的具体技术问题，例如如何修复微分方程错误，以及如何通过脚本实现实时调试和模型构建。他还详细介绍了Bloxi的工作原理和使用方法，提供了视频演示和GitHub链接，方便他人使用和改进。

• 争议的焦点可能在于Matlab和Simulink的实际应用效率以及是否有更好的替代工具。虽然[kaamuli]指出了手动操作的低效，但[stochtastic]则强调了Matlab和Simulink在某些领域的不可替代性，反映了不同用户在使用体验上的差异。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，[kaamuli]提到MathWorks正在开发类似功能，这表明该工具的潜在价值和市场需求，同时也可能引发对竞争和创新的讨论。

• 最后，[kaamuli]的分享行为和开源精神也值得关注，他不仅提供了工具，还详细说明了使用方法和开发过程，促进了技术社区的合作与进步。

Before I start - Yes, I know the differential equation in the video is wrong. I’ve already fixed it by tweaking the prompt and the script so the inputs depend on what’s being asked. The original issue was that blocks like Sum were being pasted in without matching the right number of inputs and outputs.
I’m a 2nd-year aero-engineering student at Imperial College London, I enjoy problem solving (did BPhO - gold and UKMT Gold) I'm a full-stack dev (or atleast trying to be lol) who hacked together Bloxi, an AI copilot that sits on top of Simulink and turns plain-English prompts into working control-system models and can easily debug them in real time. I felt the pain myself this term, watching top-tier students burn hours wiring blocks instead of engineering. With today’s multimodal LLMs finally able to “see” diagrams, this is the first moment an assistant like Bloxi can exist and the fastest way to give millions of engineers the same productivity leap coders just got.I built this mainly to get comfortable with LLMs and “prompt-engineering,” and I think I’ve hit the point where I’m done tinkering—especially now that MathWorks have announced they’re working on their own version. So I figured I’d share what I’ve got in case anyone wants to take it further and also just to like give it out to the world innit.
How it works:
Two scripts + simple backend (3):
One builds the Simulink model.
The other handles the chat + simple UI.
Backend that glues together the OpenAI API and frontend
Drop in your own OpenAI API key and you’re off. I used it to debug and build a few uni-project models, and it’s been surprisingly handy.
At first it just spat out a finished Simulink file, but I wanted that ChatGPT “walk-through” vibe make it feel 'magical'. So I added a couple of for loops: one to drop in blocks step-by-step, and another to wire them up.
Since raw code isn’t visible in Simulink (to the best of my knowledge), within one of my scripts I had it walk through the simulink file and screenshot each stage leveraging the fact openAI's API is multimodal, pipe them through the LLM, and let it spot inconsistencies. Works better than I expected. Perhaps someone can do better or find a better way?
Youtube video of me using it is
https://youtu.be/TX0fviaFSyg
To use download & open scripts then just do openChatbox().

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：逻辑编程的各种实现和应用

不同观点：
• [sundarurfriend] 认为 Brachylog 作为一种高尔夫语言，提供了非常愉悦的编程体验，尤其是在解决问题的过程中采用不同寻常的思维方式，但这种体验可能与用于实际编码的逻辑编程不同。
• [kragen] 推荐 miniKanren 和 microKanren，并认为通过实现 microKanren 可以获得极大的教育价值，同时指出 Datalog 更适合用于数据库的深入研究，而不是逻辑编程。
• [philzook] 提到了一种简单的 Datalog 实现，并展示了如何通过 SQL 风格的实现获得性能和功能上的提升，同时分享了一个从 Z3 AST 到 sqlite 的 Datalog 实现。
• [ashton314] 分享了自己实现 miniKanren 的详细过程，并提到实现了一个小型类型检查器，可以通过逆向运行生成符合给定类型的程序。
• [xelxebar] 推荐了一个用 Prolog 实现的窗口管理器，并表示通过使用该项目成功学习了 Prolog，同时寻求更多高质量逻辑编程代码库的阅读推荐。
• [deosjr] 分享了自己使用 miniKanren、Datalog 和 WebAssembly 实现 Bret Victor's Dynamicland 的经验，认为掌握小型逻辑编程语言的实现是一种强大的能力。
• [tracnar] 提到一个用 Soufflé 实现的逻辑编程项目，虽然觉得很有趣，但还没有找到实际应用的借口。
• [scapbi] 提到在 Mochi 项目中添加逻辑编程层的经验，利用 OpenAI Codex 生成了一个工作中的 Datalog 引擎，并提供了详细的实现过程和代码链接。
• [xlii] 分享了自己对 Prolog 实现和 Constraint Handling Rules 的研究，并提到了 CLIPS，认为这是一个很有前途的项目，特别是对于规则解析的快速支持和易于集成。
• [jpfr] 认为 miniKanren 等项目虽然不错，但正在形成一种单一文化，忽略了其他方法，并提到构建 Warren's Abstract Machine (WAM) 是 Prolog 实现的传统入门项目。
• [fracus] 认为应该从一个具体问题出发，描述逻辑编程如何比其他范式更好地解决该问题。
• [michae2] 对 Datalog 中添加整数和字符串的支持表示关注，担心这会影响查询评估的终止保证，并寻求解决方案。
• [IamDaedalus] 表示对 Prolog 的兴趣，并计划在周末尝试。
• [kriro] 对 Prolog 有深厚感情，但提到其实际使用中可能导致代码的“混乱”，并询问嵌入 Kanren 是否是推荐的做法，同时表达了对 Prolog 现状的兴趣。
• [usgroup] 认为 Prolog 似乎陷入了被遗忘和重新发现的循环。

补充讨论：
• 逻辑编程在不同项目和语言中的具体实现和应用，如 Brachylog、miniKanren、microKanren、Datalog 和 Prolog。
• 对 Datalog 中添加新功能（如整数和字符串）的技术挑战和解决方案的探讨。
• 逻辑编程在实际项目中的使用经验和教育价值，以及对高质量逻辑编程代码库的需求。
• Prolog 的历史和现状，以及其在开发者社区中的周期性兴趣。

• [ashton314] 分享了自己实现 miniKanren 的详细过程，并提到实现了一个小型类型检查器，可以通过逆向运行生成符合给定类型的程序。
• [xelxebar] 推荐了一个用 Prolog 实现的窗口管理器，并表示通过使用该项目成功学习了 Prolog，同时寻求更多高质量逻辑编程代码库的阅读推荐。
• [deosjr] 分享了自己使用 miniKanren、Datalog 和 WebAssembly 实现 Bret Victor's Dynamicland 的经验，认为掌握小型逻辑编程语言的实现是一种强大的能力。
• [tracnar] 提到一个用 Soufflé 实现的逻辑编程项目，虽然觉得很有趣，但还没有找到实际应用的借口。
• [scapbi] 提到在 Mochi 项目中添加逻辑编程层的经验，利用 OpenAI Codex 生成了一个工作中的 Datalog 引擎，并提供了详细的实现过程和代码链接。
• [xlii] 分享了自己对 Prolog 实现和 Constraint Handling Rules 的研究，并提到了 CLIPS，认为这是一个很有前途的项目，特别是对于规则解析的快速支持和易于集成。
• [jpfr] 认为 miniKanren 等项目虽然不错，但正在形成一种单一文化，忽略了其他方法，并提到构建 Warren's Abstract Machine (WAM) 是 Prolog 实现的传统入门项目。
• [fracus] 认为应该从一个具体问题出发，描述逻辑编程如何比其他范式更好地解决该问题。
• [michae2] 对 Datalog 中添加整数和字符串的支持表示关注，担心这会影响查询评估的终止保证，并寻求解决方案。
• [IamDaedalus] 表示对 Prolog 的兴趣，并计划在周末尝试。
• [kriro] 对 Prolog 有深厚感情，但提到其实际使用中可能导致代码的“混乱”，并询问嵌入 Kanren 是否是推荐的做法，同时表达了对 Prolog 现状的兴趣。
• [usgroup] 认为 Prolog 似乎陷入了被遗忘和重新发现的循环。

• 逻辑编程在不同项目和语言中的具体实现和应用，如 Brachylog、miniKanren、microKanren、Datalog 和 Prolog。
• 对 Datalog 中添加新功能（如整数和字符串）的技术挑战和解决方案的探讨。

data.author: zdw

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：macOS 新引入的 FUSE-like API 及其对开发者工具（如 Bazel、Swift、Clang）性能的影响，以及可能的解决方案，包括缓存、模块构建、沙箱技术和新的文件格式。

不同观点：
• **comex**：提到 macOS 新引入的 FUSE-like API，但担心 Apple 编译器的缓存和内容可寻址存储（CAS）机制可能会因为隔离策略导致构建速度变慢。建议 Bazel 与 LLVM 的 CAS 集成以优化性能，或者通过显式模块构建（Swift 和 Clang）来部分解决这个问题。

• **jart**：认为 macOS 的安全机制让开发环境变得不友好，类似于 Windows Vista 后的情况。建议使用 Landlock LSM 进行沙盒化，虽然它需要大约 3 次系统调用，但速度很快。同时提到如果可以一次性发送所有映射会更好。

• **ajb**：指出文中所提的通过 NFS 实现沙盒化的结论其实早在 20 年前 Vesta 构建系统就已经采用过类似方法，暗示这种方法并不新鲜。

• **dangoodmanUT**：认为新的 ASIF 稀疏镜像格式和 macOS Tahoe 的容器化框架可以解决很多当前的问题，暗示这些技术可能是未来的解决方案。

• **o11c**：提出如果对工具二进制文件有半信任态度，可以使用 `LD_PRELOAD` 等机制拦截 `open` 等系统调用，以减少对性能的影响。但也提到使用 Go 语言可能会带来额外问题。此外，建议可以保留符号链接目录而仅删除其他文件，以优化构建过程。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是 macOS 的安全机制是否对开发者不友好，以及如何在保持安全性的同时提高开发工具的性能。
• 另一个讨论点是如何有效利用缓存和模块构建来解决隔离策略带来的性能问题。
• 不同用户提出了不同的技术解决方案，如 Landlock LSM 和 ASIF 稀疏镜像格式，显示出多样化的技术视角。

data.title: The international standard for identifying postal items
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了万国邮政联盟（UPU）的S10标准，该标准用于规范国际邮件的追踪号码格式。S10标准采用13个字符，结构包括：前两位为服务标识符，接下来八位为序列号，之后一位为校验码，最后两位为表示始发国的ISO 3166–1国家代码。服务标识符代表不同的邮政服务，如普通信件或包裹邮寄，其中EMS享有“E”前缀。国家可以对某些服务标识符规则进行调整，特别是国内邮寄或与其他国家有协议时。校验码用于纠错，通过特定算法计算。追踪号以条形码形式打印，通常使用Code 128或Code 39格式。这一标准确保了各国邮政服务之间的互通和追踪号码的一致性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于物流系统中序列号和编码标准的讨论，包括其实际容量、算法复杂性以及在不同场景下的应用。

不同观点：
• Ecco 认为中国的物流系统在处理大量包裹时可能会面临序列号不足的问题，尤其是像Shein或Temu这样的平台在短时间内产生的大量包裹，可能导致序列号用尽。
• Forth_fool 指出，8位数的序列号实际上可以产生接近1亿个唯一号码，而不是Ecco所担心的1000万，纠正了对序列号容量的误解。
• Nojs 提到文章中未提及的LPC码，并提供了参考视频，暗示可能有更具体的编码方式未被讨论。
• Bloak 讨论了复杂算法的必要性，质疑用于校验位的复杂算法是否比EAN或13位ISBN使用的简单算法更有优势。
• Lysace 表示对全球标准被广泛接受感到欣慰，认为至少在某些方面可以达成一致。

补充讨论：
• ThePowerOfFuet 提出关于DataMatrix码的问题，尤其是在杂志等邮件上出现的包含收件人全名和地址的码，询问其标准格式和用途，这与前述讨论的序列号问题有一定关联但属于不同应用场景。

争议焦点：主要争议在于序列号是否足够以及复杂算法的必要性。Ecco担心序列号可能不足，而Forth_fool则认为这种担心不必要。Bloak对复杂算法的有效性提出质疑，而Lysace则强调全球标准的一致性带来的好处。

44258633.article_content:
The International Standard for Identifying Postal Items
The Universal Postal Union's S10 standard, in all its glory
Have you ever received a parcel from overseas? I did recently, from Switzerland!
Looking at the envelope, I realised the format of the tracking number (
UT038926726CH
) was in a very similar (if not identical) format to ones I'd used frequently here in the UK.
I'd been receiving emails from Royal Mail about the parcel, so I just presumed that there was some data-sharing agreement in place with Swiss Post and Royal Mail had just given the parcel their own internal reference number.
But seeing the reference number printed on the envelope from the get-go made me want to see what Swiss Post had to say about it...
The same tracking number works across multiple carriers, and it's the same format as all the UK ones! What gives??
Enter: the United Nations Universal Postal Union
The
Universal Postal Union (UPU)
is an agency of the UN that coordinates postal policies to facilitate post flowing across the world. As part of this, it publishes the
S10 standard for the identification of postal items
in a 13-character format - ie. what we've been seeing on our parcels!
If you're interested in learning more about the UPU's interesting 150-year history, you might want to check out
this article
written by fellow webring inhabitant Imaan!
1
Each country's national postal service is assigned as having exclusive reign over S10 codes for that country, and they go about issuing S10 codes from their country.
Tracking Number Format
As it turns out, the structure of our tracking number has a strict design, and our tracking number contains four distinct things:
Character number
Format
Description
1 and 2
2 letters
Service indicator
3 to 10
8 digits
Serial number
11
1 digit
A check digit
12 and 13
2 letters
ISO 3166–1 country code representing the origin of the item
The Service Indicator
The first two characters represent the service that's been used to post the item. There's a fairly extensive list in the standard, with specific options for tracked post, letter post, parcel post... the list goes on. The most interesting part of the service indicators are threefold:
First, there are specific carve-outs in the specification for an organisation called
EMS
- they get all
E
prefixes, so
EA
,
EB
,
EC
, and so on and so forth. EMS is an express international mail service that's run by the UPU itself, but that delegates operations to the national postal services that control their country's S10 codes. This is why you'll not see any way to buy shipping using EMS directly on their website - you buy express international shipping at your local post office and they route it accordingly. It's also worth noting that this only applies to express shipping - not regular-rate traffic.
Second, countries are allowed to override some of the service indicator assignment rules set out in the S10 standard. This can happen when either a parcel is being sent domestically or when a carrier has an agreement with other countries' carriers to reassign some service indicators for other purposes, hence the inclusion of the origin country code to aid interpretation of tracking numbers where this is the case.
Lastly, some service indicators are explicitly disallowed from being used. These are
JA–JZ
,
KA–KZ
,
SA–SZ
,
TA–TZ
and
WA–WZ
since these carry the risk of causing a tracking number to be confused with codes from a different UN data encoding standard.
All in, the possible service indicator space looks like this:
Table source
The Serial Number
This is just a serial number. It's exactly 8 digits long and is generated by the originating carrier as they see fit, provided they don't resue the same number within 12 months. In theory, this means a lost parcel can only be lost for 12 months before it vanishes from the world forever, but in reality, the S10 recommends not reusing a number within a minimum period of 24 months. Even then, you have 10 million parcels per service indicator per country available to be issued, so it's probably not going to be necessary for a carrier to reuse a number for a much longer period of time anyway.
The Check Digit
The check digit corrects any errors in the serial number preceding it, using the following algorithm:
Multiply each digit in the sequence with the corresponding number from this sequence:
8 6 4 2 3 5 9 7
Sum all these values
Divide the sum by 11
Substrac the remainder from 11
If the result is in the range 1-9, use that as the checksum
If the result is 10, use 0 as the checksum
If the result is 11, use 5 as the checksum
This is not a particularly strong checksum, but it's good enough to guard against a couple of accidental digit-swaps here and there. You can play with an interactive demo of it
here
.
Barcode Format
The S10 standard requires tracking numbers to be printed on an item as a barcode, either being in
Code 128
or
Code 39
format.

data.title: Denmark Wants to Dump Microsoft Software for Linux, LibreOffice
data.author: louthy
data.article_summary: 丹麦数字事务部计划逐步淘汰微软软件，转向使用开源的Linux操作系统和LibreOffice。该过渡将从下个月开始，首先对一半员工实施，并预计在秋季完成。此举旨在节省成本并减少对美国软件的依赖，同时实现"数字主权"目标。尽管计划如此，部长Caroline Stage表示，若过渡过于复杂，可能重新使用微软产品。此前，德国一个州也宣布了类似的转型计划，而丹麦的哥本哈根和奥胡斯市也因政治因素希望摆脱微软软件，支持开源替代方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲委员会尝试摆脱像Google这样的美国科技巨头，使用如Linux和Open Office等开源软件的举措是否可行。

不同观点：
• **支持尝试，但持怀疑态度**：
   - **[p0w3n3d]** 认为，为了自由，摆脱Google等公司的控制是好的尝试。但同时预测这种尝试会失败，因为Linux和Open Office不能完全替代常规办公软件。该评论暗示了开源软件在功能或用户体验上的不足。
   
• **历史失败案例的启示**：
   - **[1oooqooq]** 提到，自1990年代末以来，类似的尝试已经被进行了无数次，但最终都失败了，例如欧洲委员会最终还是会回归微软的产品。评论还指出，单靠地方努力无法摆脱“殖民主义”式的依赖，暗示这种转变需要更广泛的系统性改变。

• **对先前讨论的引用**：
   - **[ChrisArchitect]** 没有直接表达立场，而是引用了早先的相关讨论（链接：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44234552），暗示这个问题之前已经有过深入探讨，可能没有新的突破。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：主要集中在开源软件（如Linux和Open Office）是否能够胜任常规办公工作。一方认为功能不足，无法替代现有主流软件；另一方则认为历史上的多次失败表明这种转变非常困难，可能需要更系统性的改变，而不是单纯的技术替代。

• **对失败原因的分析**：一些评论者（如[1oooqooq]）认为失败是因为缺乏足够的系统性支持和长期坚持，将其比喻为无法通过地方努力摆脱“殖民主义”。

• **对开源软件的态度**：虽然有人支持开源软件的理念，但对其在实际工作中的可行性表示怀疑，特别是在面对已经成熟的商业软件时。

总体来看，讨论围绕着开源软件替代主流商业软件的可行性、历史失败的教训以及更深层次的系统性变革需求展开。

44273056.article_content:
A government ministry in Denmark is preparing to phase out Microsoft software and switch to the open-source Linux and LibreOffice.
The country’s Ministry for Digital Affairs will kick off the transition next month by dumping Windows and
Microsoft 365
, starting first with half of its employees. “If everything goes as expected, all employees will be on an open-source solution during the autumn,” Danish news outlet
Politiken
reports.
The change promises to save on costs and reduce the ministry’s dependency on US software. Denmark’s Minister for Digital Affairs, Caroline Stage, tells Politiken that "digital sovereignty" is now a priority under the ministry’s new four-year digitalization strategy.
Recommended by Our Editors
Microsoft Extends Support for Office Apps on Windows 10 for 3 More Years
44 Excel Tips for Becoming a Spreadsheet Pro
Not Just Skype: Microsoft Is Killing This 34-Year-Old App, Too
The decision will also help the ministry avoid the costly undertaking of managing computers on Windows 10, which
loses official support in October
. However, Stage is leaving some leeway for the ministry to reverse course. “If phasing out proves to be too complicated, we can revert back to Microsoft in an instant,” she says.
Last year, a German state office
announced
a similar effort to transition 30,000 employees to Linux and LibreOffice.
In Denmark’s case, two other major cities, Copenhagen and Aarhus, also want to phase out Microsoft software. Both municipalities
cited
President Trump's
contentious stance
toward Europe as a reason. Politicians in the country have also been calling for reducing Denmark’s dependence on US tech companies in favor of backing open-source alternatives.

• **对先前讨论的引用**：
   - **[ChrisArchitect]** 没有直接表达立场，而是引用了早先的相关讨论（链接：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44234552），暗示这个问题之前已经有过深入探讨，可能没有新的突破。

补充讨论：

• **对失败原因的分析**：一些评论者（如[1oooqooq]）认为失败是因为缺乏足够的系统性支持和长期坚持，将其比喻为无法通过地方努力摆脱“殖民主义”。

• **对开源软件的态度**：虽然有人支持开源软件的理念，但对其在实际工作中的可行性表示怀疑，特别是在面对已经成熟的商业软件时。

data.title: Peano arithmetic is enough, because Peano arithmetic  encodes computation
data.author: btilly
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了在皮亚诺算术（PA）中是否能够证明每个Goodstein序列最终都会到达零。Goodstein序列是一个数列，起始于某个自然数，通过逐步替换基数并减一来生成。已知PA可以证明任何特定的Goodstein序列实例最终会到达零，但无法证明对所有自然数的通用情况。

文章探讨了是否可以在PA中证明以下命题：
$$ \forall n \in \mathbb{N}: \exists p \in \mathbb{N}: P_{\mathrm{PA}}(p, \ulcorner G(n)\urcorner) $$
即，对于每个自然数$n$，存在一个PA中的证明$p$，证明$G(n)$（即起始于$n$的Goodstein序列最终会到达零）。

尽管PA不能证明Goodstein定理的通用情况，但有评论者指出，PA实际上足以证明每个特定实例，因为可以通过计算足够的序列项来验证。然而，完整的证明通常依赖于更强的系统（如ZF集合论）。

文章最后提到，PA是足够的，因为它能够编码计算过程，并通过类似Lisp的编程逻辑展示如何在PA中实现这种证明。这需要复杂的推理和编码技术，但理论上是可行的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Peano公理（PA）的讨论，包括其限制、应用以及与其他数学和计算理论的关系。

不同观点：
• btilly介绍了一个博客帖子，解释了Peano公理的限制以及如何在Peano公理基础上引导Lisp。特别提到帖子包含了一些玩笑。
• Animats指出，这与Boyer-Moore理论相似，该理论从Peano公理层面构建数学。他还提供了一个GNU Common LISP的自动化定理证明器链接。
• dwohnitmok纠正了在Math Stackexchange上的一个评论，强调了标准自然数模型的重要性，并解释了如果PA证明了“PA证明X”，那么PA也能证明X。
• dooglius对Goodstein定理的独立性及其在PA中的证明方式感兴趣，认为PA加上“PA是一致的”可能足以证明Goodstein定理，并能进行超限归纳。
• cryptonector认为纯lambda演算足够，因为lambda演算编码了计算。
• gugagore提到Peano公理并不是唯一的设计选择，强调了不把Peano公理视为固有重要性是有益的。

• RossBencina质疑仅依赖计算是否足够，指出可计算实数是实数的一个子集。
• zozbot234幽默地提到Peano算术足够，但仅限于处理到88的范围，引用了一张图片作为玩笑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于Peano公理的限制和应用范围，特别是在证明有限性和处理非标准模型方面的能力。
• 讨论中提到了多个外部资源和链接，如Boyer-Moore理论的文献、自动化定理证明器的代码库、视频讲解等，为深入理解相关内容提供了参考。
• 讨论中还涉及了对Peano公理的哲学思考，如gugagore提出的Peano公理是否是唯一的或最基础的选择。

这些观点展示了Peano公理在数学和计算理论中的多方面应用和讨论，涉及理论的细节、证明的有效性以及实际应用中的局限性。

$\begingroup$
This is one of a pair of questions trying to understand
this comment
on the xkcd forum contest
My number is bigger than yours!
. For a definition of Goodstein sequences, see
this question
.
Let
$G(n)$
be a formula that says "the Goodstein sequence starting with
$n$
eventually reaches
$0$
". Now, it is known that Peano arithmetic (
$\mathrm{PA}$
) can prove any particular instance
$G(n)$
where
$n$
is a "standard" natural number (e.g.
$15$
,
$268$
, etc.), but it cannot prove
$\forall n \in \mathbb{N}: G(n)$
.
The proof in
$\mathrm{PA}$
for any particular instance isn't difficult: just calculate enough terms of the sequence until it reaches
$0$
. But we only know this always works (and know how many terms to calculate) thanks to a stronger system (such as
$\mathrm{ZF}$
) that can prove Goodstein's theorem.
Now, the comment author claims that in fact, this can be proven using
$\mathrm{PA}$
itself. I find that dubious, since the simple argument above does not go through. But perhaps there is some way to use parts of the
proof
of Goodstein's theorem that are accessible to
$\mathrm{PA}$
(using ordinal numbers up to, but not including,
$\varepsilon_0$
).
Just to clarify the question, let us use the notation
$P_{\mathrm{PA}}(p, \ulcorner\phi\urcorner)$
to mean "
$p$
codes for the proof of
$\phi$
in
$\mathrm{PA}$
". Then my question is what system we need to prove:
$$
\forall n \in \mathbb{N}: \exists p \in \mathbb{N}: P_{\mathrm{PA}}(p, \ulcorner G(n)\urcorner)
$$
Is
$\mathrm{PA}$
enough, or do we need a stronger system, e.g.
$\mathrm{ZF}$
?

data.title: Filedb: Disk-based key-value store inspired by Bitcask
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: FileDB 是一个受 Bitcask 启发的键值存储系统，使用 Zig 语言实现。它通过日志结构的哈希表存储记录元数据，并以仅追加模式将记录插入到一个磁盘文件中。当文件达到上限或重启时，文件会轮转，旧文件只读。FileDB 定期进行压缩，将多个文件合并为一个并更新元数据。它通过保持文件打开实现高吞吐量，元数据存储使记录获取成为 O(1) 操作。FileDB 还提供了与 Redis 兼容的客户端，并展示了较高的请求处理速度和较低的延迟。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bitcask及其在键值存储中的应用与比较

不同观点：
• [b0a04gl] 认为Bitcask简单有效，特别适合需要高性能写入和持久化但不要求范围查询或索引的项目。他提到Bitcask避免了复杂的抽象和过多的优化，通过简单的设计实现了稳定性能，并且在面对数据增长时启动时间不会显著增加。

• [im_down_w_otp] 指出Bitcask缺乏良好的二级索引策略，导致在需要二级索引的场景中不如LevelDB。尽管在Riak中使用Bitcask可以获得高性能和一致性，但二级索引的需求常常让开发者选择LevelDB后端。

• [lsferreira42] 分享了自己的一个类似项目，一个带有标签搜索功能的磁盘键值存储，展示了在键值存储实现上的不同设计选择。

• [wallstop] 对设计中把`sync`功能交给客户端实现表示担忧，认为这样可能会导致数据丢失，质疑这种设计选择对文件完整性的影响。

• [Imustaskforhelp] 表达了对各种数据库技术的广泛兴趣，并希望获得简单易懂的解释。他将Bitcask与其他数据库（如Redis、SQLite、PostgreSQL、ClickHouse、DuckDB、Turso、Cloudflare D1）进行比较，寻求在不同场景下使用Bitcask的建议。

补充讨论：
• Bitcask的简洁设计和低复杂度是其主要优点，但在需要高级功能（如二级索引）时可能不如其他解决方案。
• 对设计中数据完整性和`sync`功能的讨论，反映了对可靠性和数据安全性的关注。
• 不同用户对Bitcask的应用场景和与其他数据库的比较表现出多样化的兴趣，特别是对新手友好的解释和使用建议。

filedb
A key-value store inspired by Bitcask.
FileDB is a Zig-implementation of Bitcask by Riak
1
paper.
FileDB stores record metadata in a log-structured hashtable and parallely keeps 1 disk file open for inserting records in append-only mode. On restarts or
MAX_FILE_REACHED
, the disk file is rotated and all the oldfiles are kept open for reading
only
.
A compaction process running every
config.compactionInterval
seconds, reads all the disk files and combines them into one file while updating the metadata hashtable.
A sync process syncs the open disk files once every
config.syncInterval
. Sync also can be done on every request if
config.alwaysFsync
is True.
Read about internals in-depth at
FileDb
.
Benefits:
Since the metadata keeps an exact location of file and position in file for a record, fetching records become O(1) operation.
All metadata records are constant size, so irrespective of the size of the value of a record the in-memory store keeps a constant sized metadata.
Provides high throughput by using the open file in append only mode.

• [b0a04gl] 认为Bitcask简单有效，特别适合需要高性能写入和持久化但不要求范围查询或索引的项目。他提到Bitcask避免了复杂的抽象和过多的优化，通过简单的设计实现了稳定性能，并且在面对数据增长时启动时间不会显著增加。

• [im_down_w_otp] 指出Bitcask缺乏良好的二级索引策略，导致在需要二级索引的场景中不如LevelDB。尽管在Riak中使用Bitcask可以获得高性能和一致性，但二级索引的需求常常让开发者选择LevelDB后端。

• [lsferreira42] 分享了自己的一个类似项目，一个带有标签搜索功能的磁盘键值存储，展示了在键值存储实现上的不同设计选择。

• [wallstop] 对设计中把`sync`功能交给客户端实现表示担忧，认为这样可能会导致数据丢失，质疑这种设计选择对文件完整性的影响。

• [Imustaskforhelp] 表达了对各种数据库技术的广泛兴趣，并希望获得简单易懂的解释。他将Bitcask与其他数据库（如Redis、SQLite、PostgreSQL、ClickHouse、DuckDB、Turso、Cloudflare D1）进行比较，寻求在不同场景下使用Bitcask的建议。

补充讨论：
• Bitcask的简洁设计和低复杂度是其主要优点，但在需要高级功能（如二级索引）时可能不如其他解决方案。
• 对设计中数据完整性和`sync`功能的讨论，反映了对可靠性和数据安全性的关注。
• 不同用户对Bitcask的应用场景和与其他数据库的比较表现出多样化的兴趣，特别是对新手友好的解释和使用建议。

am co-hosting this event
with the wonderful
convoke.bio
from 6:30pm-8:30pm on June 24th. Location TBD, but it will be in SF! You should come! Also, extremely grateful to
Shilpa Pothapragada
for both inspiring + reviewing this essay.
Introduction
Why is endometriosis interesting?
The primary hypothesis of why it exists is not complete
It is nearly equivalent to cancer
There is no (real) cure to it
There are few diseases on Earth as widespread and underfunded as it is
Conclusion
Introduction
There are several diseases that are canonically recognized as ‘
interesting
’, even by laymen. Whether that is in their mechanism of action, their impact on the patient, or something else entirely. It’s hard to tell
exactly
what makes a medical condition interesting, it’s a you-know-it-when-you-see-it sort of thing.
One such example is measles. Measles is an unremarkable disease based solely on its clinical progression: fever, malaise, coughing, and a relatively low death rate of 0.2%~. What
is
astonishing about the disease is its capacity to infect cells of the adaptive immune system (memory B‑ and T-cells). This means that if you do end up surviving measles,
you are left with an immune system not dissimilar to one of a just-born infant,
entirely naive to polio, diphtheria, pertussis, and every single other infection you received protection against either via vaccines or natural infection. It can take up to 3 years for one's ‘immune memory’ to return, prior to which you are entirely immunocompromised.
There’s a wide range of such diseases, each one their own unique horror. Others include rabies (t
rans-synaptic transmission
), ebola (
causes your blood vessels to become porous
), tetanus (
causes muscle contractions so strong that they can break bones
), and so on.
Very few people would instinctively pigeonhole endometriosis as something similarly
physiologically
interesting, or at least I wouldn’t have. But via a mutual friend, I recently had a chat with
Shilpa Pothapragada
, a Schmidt Fellow studying at the Wyss Institute at Harvard. She studies better ways to diagnose endometriosis, and, as a result of the fascinating conversation, I now consider the disease one of the strangest conditions I’ve ever heard of.
Honestly, prior to my discussion with Shilpa, I didn’t even know what endometriosis even
was,
only that it was painful to have and affects women. To judge whether I was simply deeply ignorant, or the disease genuinely didn’t have much mindshare, I took an informal poll amongst a dozen friends outside of the life-sciences. Even amongst cisgender women (!), knowledge of what endometriosis was
astonishingly
sparse — most people could only say something like ‘
that’s a uterus condition, right?
’, and a sum total of zero people actually knew what the disease entailed.
So I decided to write this essay in an attempt to fix that knowledge gap amongst the small population of people who follow me.
Why is endometriosis interesting?
But, before we get to my points: what actually
is
the clinical definition of endometriosis?
Plainly put, it is when tissue that resembles the uterine lining, or endometrial-like tissue, grows outside the uterus. The tissue can implant itself in nearby tissues, like the ovaries and fallopian tubes, or even more distal organs like the bladder and bowel. Due to the continuous influx of hormonal growth factors (mainly estrogen), these misplaced endometrial-like cells respond cyclically, just as the normal uterine lining does. They thicken, break down, and bleed with each menstrual cycle, but unlike the uterine lining,
they have nowhere to go.
Instead of exiting through menstruation, this trapped tissue and blood accumulates, causing severe pain, inflammation, fibrosis (scar formation), and adhesion between organs. Over time, these repeated cycles of inflammation and fibrosis may lead to permanent structural changes within the abdomen and pelvis, contributing to chronic pelvic pain and infertility.
To segue into the first interesting aspect of the disease, how did the tissue
get
there in the first place? What caused it to be trapped? Well, it’s a curious question, because…
The primary hypothesis of why it exists is not complete
Retrograde menstruation
is perhaps the most culturally dominant theory as to why endometriosis occurs at all, first proposed by gynecologist John Sampson nearly 100 years ago. The theory is straightforward: during menstruation, some sloughed-off endometrial cells flow backward through the fallopian tubes into the pelvic cavity instead of outward through the cervix. data.title: SIMD-friendly algorithms for substring searching (2018)
data.author: Rendello
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了利用SIMD指令进行子字符串搜索的算法，旨在提高在现代CPU上的搜索效率。传统算法假设字符比较代价高，但现代CPU通过SIMD指令可以并行比较多个字节，从而使简单比较比复杂的DFA算法更高效。

文章提出了三种SIMD友好算法：

1. **通用SIMD算法**：使用SIMD比较子字符串的首尾字符，生成潜在匹配位置的掩码，再进行精确比较。
2. **SSE特定算法（MPSADBW）**：利用SSE指令进行快速子字符串匹配。
3. **SSE4.2特定算法（PCMPESTRM）**：使用SSE4.2指令进行高效字符串搜索。

这些算法通过并行比较字符和避免函数调用开销，显著提高了性能。文中提供了不同架构（如SSE、AVX2、AVX512F、ARM Neon）的实现和性能测试结果，展示了SIMD指令在子字符串搜索中的优势。通过专门优化，子字符串比较的代价可以大幅降低。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同开发者对字符串搜索算法及其实现的讨论，尤其是使用SIMD（单指令多数据）优化搜索性能的各类方法和工具。

不同观点：
• **burntsushi的观点**：ripgrep通过AVX2和泛型方法加速搜索，尤其是通过Rust的`regex`库。其优化算法通过启发式选择频率较低的两个字节来加速搜索，相比传统的Two-Way算法和GNU libc的`memmem`实现更快。他还指出，某些API由于每次都需要重建搜索状态，导致效率低下，特别是当针（needle）在多次搜索中保持不变时。

• **ncruces的观点**：在Wasm/WASI libc的SIMD优化中实现了类似的方法，并指出对于已知的长 haystack 和大的 needle，Quick Search 方法非常有效。他还提供了自己的实现链接。

• **mwsherman的观点**：提到C#中已经为`IndexOf`实现了某些SIMD优化，并提供了相关实现的链接。

• **clauderoux的观点**：分享了自己在使用SMID方法进行字符串搜索和分割的多种算法实现，并提供了一个不同的算法实现链接。

• **klaussilveira的观点**：提到一个用于快速HTTP解析的SIMD算法库`hparse`，与讨论中的算法有相似之处。

• **eska的观点**：指出swar算法由于将1字节对齐的数据转换为8字节对齐，可能存在未定义行为（UB），并可能因此导致性能问题。

• **rurban的观点**：认为libc的`strstr`性能不佳，但musl库表现优异，并建议为高效算法命名并进行对比测试。

• **mgaunard的观点**：提到2018年的缺失部分，可能暗示某些历史实现未被讨论。

• **sylware的观点**：关注SIMD方法在不同字符串大小下的效率问题，指出对于小字符串，SIMD的设置代码可能比基本的字节搜索更昂贵，且性能依赖于硬件架构。

• **azhenley的观点**：希望能够在Python中直接使用SIMD，而不需要调用其他语言。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是不同算法在实际应用中的效率，尤其是对于不同大小的字符串和硬件架构的表现。
- 另一个值得注意的点是API设计对性能的影响，特别是当搜索的针在多次调用中不变时，重建状态的代价。
- 开发者们分享了多个相关实现和优化算法的链接，展示了社区中多种解决方案的共存和竞争。

SIMD-friendly algorithms for substring searching
Author:
Wojciech MuÅa
Added on:
2016-11-28
Updated on:
2018-02-14 (spelling), 2017-04-29 (ARMv8 results)
Introduction
Popular programming languages provide methods or functions which locate a
substring in a given string. In C it is the function
strstr
, the C++
class
std::string
has the method
find
, Python's
string
has methods
pos
and
index
, and so on, so forth. All these APIs were designed for
one-shot searches
.  During past decades several algorithms to solve this
problem were designed, an excellent page by
Christian Charras
and
Thierry Lecroq
lists most of them
(if not all). Basically these
algorithms could be split into two major categories: (1) based on
Deterministic Finite Automaton, like Knuth-Morris-Pratt, Boyer Moore, etc.,
and (2) based on a simple comparison, like the Karp-Rabin algorithm.
The main problem with these standard algorithms is a silent assumption
that comparing a pair of characters, looking up in an extra table and
conditions are cheap, while comparing two substrings is expansive.
But current desktop CPUs do not meet this assumption, in particular:
There is no difference in comparing one, two, four or 8 bytes on a 64-bit
CPU.  When a processor supports SIMD instructions, then comparing vectors
(it means 16, 32 or even 64 bytes) is as cheap as comparing a single byte.
Thus comparing short sequences of chars can be faster than fancy algorithms
which avoids such comparison.
Looking up in a table costs one memory fetch, so at least a L1 cache round
(~3 cycles). Reading char-by-char also cost as much cycles.
Mispredicted jumps cost several cycles of penalty (~10-20 cycles).
There is a short chain of dependencies: read char, compare it, conditionally
jump, which make hard to utilize out-of-order execution capabilities present
in a CPU.

44274001.article_summary:
本文讨论了利用SIMD指令进行子字符串搜索的算法，旨在提高在现代CPU上的搜索效率。传统算法假设字符比较代价高，但现代CPU通过SIMD指令可以并行比较多个字节，从而使简单比较比复杂的DFA算法更高效。

文章提出了三种SIMD友好算法：

1. **通用SIMD算法**：使用SIMD比较子字符串的首尾字符，生成潜在匹配位置的掩码，再进行精确比较。
2. **SSE特定算法（MPSADBW）**：利用SSE指令进行快速子字符串匹配。
3. **SSE4.2特定算法（PCMPESTRM）**：使用SSE4.2指令进行高效字符串搜索。

这些算法通过并行比较字符和避免函数调用开销，显著提高了性能。文中提供了不同架构（如SSE、AVX2、AVX512F、ARM Neon）的实现和性能测试结果，展示了SIMD指令在子字符串搜索中的优势。通过专门优化，子字符串比较的代价可以大幅降低。

主要讨论点：不同开发者对字符串搜索算法及其实现的讨论，尤其是使用SIMD（单指令多数据）优化搜索性能的各类方法和工具。

不同观点：
• **burntsushi的观点**：ripgrep通过AVX2和泛型方法加速搜索，尤其是通过Rust的`regex`库。其优化算法通过启发式选择频率较低的两个字节来加速搜索，相比传统的Two-Way算法和GNU libc的`memmem`实现更快。他还指出，某些API由于每次都需要重建搜索状态，导致效率低下，特别是当针（needle）在多次搜索中保持不变时。

• **ncruces的观点**：在Wasm/WASI libc的SIMD优化中实现了类似的方法，并指出对于已知的长 haystack 和大的 needle，Quick Search 方法非常有效。他还提供了自己的实现链接。

• **mwsherman的观点**：提到C#中已经为`IndexOf`实现了某些SIMD优化，并提供了相关实现的链接。

data.author: cirwin
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Go语言正在开发的“Green Tea”垃圾回收器。当前Go的垃圾回收器使用经典的三色并行标记算法，但该算法未考虑内存位置，导致空间局部性、时间局部性差，且忽略了拓扑结构。随着CPU核心数量增加和非均匀内存架构的普及，这一问题愈发严重。Green Tea算法通过以更大、连续的内存块（称为"spans"）为单位进行扫描，提高内存访问的局部性，减少CPU在扫描循环中的停滞时间。该算法已在原型中实现，并在基准测试中显示出对GC重负载工作量的CPU成本显著降低。文章还讨论了未来可能的优化方向，如SIMD加速。Green Tea计划作为可选实验功能在Go 1.25中引入。

补充讨论：
- **GC性能的优化范围**：新GC机制在特定微基准测试中表现良好，但在更广泛的基准测试中可能存在轻微性能下降。

Green Tea 🍵 Garbage Collector
Authors: Michael Knyszek, Austin Clements
Updated: 2 May 2025
This issue tracks the design and implementation of the Green Tea garbage collector. As of the last update to this issue, development of Green Tea is still active. We'll produce more detailed design document once we're ready to commit to a design. For now, Green Tea is available as an experiment at tip-of-tree and is planned as to be available as an opt-in experiment in Go 1.25, once it releases. We encourage teams to
try it out
.
Introduction
Memory latency and bandwidth are becoming increasingly constrained as CPU clocks outpace DRAM clocks, increasing core counts offer more load on physically limited memory buses, and speed-of-light constraints necessitate increasingly non-uniform memory topologies. As a result, spatial locality, temporal locality, and topology-awareness are becoming ever more critical to high-performance systems.
Unfortunately, all of these trends are at odds with most of today’s garbage collection algorithms.
Go’s garbage collector
implements a classic tri-color parallel marking algorithm. This is, at its core, just a graph flood, where heap objects are nodes in the graph, and pointers are edges. However, this graph flood affords no consideration to the memory location of the objects that are being processed. As a result, it exhibits extremely poor spatial locality—jumping between completely different parts of memory—poor temporal locality—blithely spreading repeated accesses to the same memory across the GC cycle—and no concern for topology.
As a result, on average 85% of the garbage collector's time is spent in the core loop of this graph flood—the scan loop—and >35% of CPU cycles in the scan loop are spent solely stalled on memory accesses, excluding any knock-on effects. This problem is expected to only get worse as the industry trends toward many-core systems and non-uniform memory architectures.
In this document, we present Green Tea: a parallel marking algorithm that, if not memory-centric,
1
is at least
memory-aware
, in that it endeavors to process objects close to one another together.
This new algorithm has
an implementation
that is ready for developers to trial on their workloads, and in this document we also present the results from evaluating this implementation against our benchmark suite. Overall, the algorithm shows a significant reduction in GC CPU costs on GC-heavy workloads.
Finally, this new marking algorithm unlocks new opportunities for future optimization, such as SIMD acceleration, which we discuss with other possible avenues of future work.
Design
The core idea behind the new parallel marking algorithm is simple. Instead of scanning individual objects, the garbage collector scans memory in much larger, contiguous blocks. The shared work queue tracks these coarse blocks instead of individual objects, and the individual objects waiting to be scanned in a block are tracked in that block itself. The core hypothesis is that while a block waits on the queue to be scanned, it will accumulate more objects to be scanned within that block, such that when a block does get dequeued, it’s likely that scanning will be able to scan more than one object in that block. This, in turn, improves locality of memory access, in addition to better amortizing per-scan costs.
Prototype implementation
In the prototype implementation of this new algorithm, the memory blocks we track are called
spans
. A span is always some multiple of 8 KiB, always aligned to 8 KiB, and consists entirely of objects of one size. Our prototype focuses exclusively on “small object spans”, which are exactly 8 KiB and contain objects up to 512 bytes.
A span is also the basic unit of storing heap metadata. In the prototype, each span stores two bits for each object: a
gray
bit and a
black
bit. These correspond to the tri-color abstraction: an object is
black
if it has been scanned,
gray
if it is in the queue to be scanned, and
white
if it has not been reached at all. In the prototype, white objects have neither bit set, gray objects have the gray bit set, and black objects have both bits set.

data.title: Slowing the flow of core-dump-related CVEs
data.author: jwilk
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Linux内核在处理崩溃进程的核心转储（core dump）时存在的安全问题及改进措施。核心转储用于记录进程崩溃时的状态，但其处理机制长期以来导致了许多安全漏洞（CVEs）。当前的问题在于，核心转储处理程序作为用户模式助手，以完全特权运行，成为攻击目标。攻击者可以通过竞争条件漏洞，利用崩溃进程的PID替换，获取敏感信息如`/etc/shadow`文件内容。为解决此问题，6.16内核引入了改进措施，包括新增格式标识符`%F`，使处理程序能够通过pidfd准确识别崩溃的进程，从而减少此类漏洞。文章强调需要更安全的API来处理核心转储。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux系统中核心转储（core dump）机制的设计缺陷及其安全与实用性问题

不同观点：
• inopinatus提到一个历史事件，通过利用核心转储处理不当的情况解决了实际问题，这可能暗示了核心转储机制在早期存在实际可利用的漏洞，带有一定的怀旧和技术分享色彩。

• 10000truths认为Linux核心转储机制存在设计缺陷，主要问题在于其作为全局设置且只能由root用户访问。他建议通过命名空间隔离或委派给reaper/subreaper进程来改进设计，并提到社区曾讨论过这些想法，但似乎未有实质进展。他提供了相关讨论链接以支持其观点。

• mort96对讨论中出现的"**** API"表示困惑，不确定其真实含义，质疑这是否意味着API存在问题，还是仅表达了作者的一种情绪。这反映出讨论中用词不清可能导致的误解问题。

• DeepYogurt简短地指出，CVE（常见漏洞与暴露）推动设计变革是好事，暗示安全问题确实促进了核心转储机制的改进。

• charcircuit深入探讨了核心转储处理以用户模式助手方式运行的问题，质疑为何不以专用核心转储用户身份运行。他还提到核心转储套接字传递给助手功能存在的漏洞，并对其在容器环境中的实用性提出质疑，认为共享崩溃报告基础设施可能更合理。

补充讨论：
• 核心转储机制的全局性和权限问题成为讨论焦点，不同用户对设计缺陷的严重性和改进方向有不同看法。

• charcircuit对核心转储在容器环境中的应用提出进一步的技术和安全质疑，拓展了讨论的范围。

Slowing the flow of core-dump-related CVEs
[LWN subscriber-only content]
Welcome to LWN.net
The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this
article, please consider
subscribing to LWN
.  Thank you
for visiting LWN.net!
By
Jonathan Corbet
June 6, 2025
The 6.16 kernel will include a number of changes to how the kernel handles
the processing of core dumps for crashed processes.  Christian Brauner
explained
his reasons for doing this work as: "
Because I'm a clown and also I had
it with all the CVEs because we provide a **** API for userspace
".  The
handling of core dumps has indeed been a constant source of
vulnerabilities; with luck, the 6.16 work will result in rather fewer of
them in the future.
The problem with core dumps
A core dump is an image of a process's data areas — everything except the
executable text; it can be used to investigate the cause of a crash by
examining a process's state at the time things went wrong.  Once upon a
time, Unix systems would routinely place a core dump into a file called
core
in the current working directory when a program crashed.  The
main effects of this practice were to inspire system administrators
worldwide to remove
core
files daily via
cron
jobs, and
to make it hazardous to use the name
core
for anything you wanted
to keep.  Linux systems can still create
core
files, but are
usually configured not to.
An alternative that
is
used on some systems is to have the kernel
launch a process to read the core dump from a crashing process and,
presumably, do something useful with it.  This behavior is configured by
writing an appropriate string to
the
core_pattern
sysctl knob
.  A number of distributors use this
mechanism to set up core-dump handlers that phone home to report crashes so
that the guilty programs can, hopefully, be fixed.
This is the "
**** API
" referred to by Brauner; it indeed has a
number of problems.  For example, the core-dump handler is launched by the
kernel as a user-mode helper, meaning that it runs fully privileged in the
root namespace.  That, needless to say, makes it an attractive target for
attackers.  There are also a number of race conditions that emerge from this
design that have led to vulnerabilities of their own.
See, for example,
this recent
Qualys advisory
describing a vulnerability in Ubuntu's
apport
tool and the
systemd-coredump
utility, both of which are designed to process core dumps.  In short, an
attacker starts by running a setuid binary, then forcing it to crash at an
opportune moment.  While the core-dump handler is being launched (a step
that the attacker can delay in various ways), the crashed process is killed
outright with a
SIGKILL
signal, then quickly replaced by another
process with the same process ID.  The core-dump handler will then begin to
examine the core dump from the crashed process, but with the information
from the replacement process.
That process is running in its own attacker-crafted namespace, with some
strategic environmental changes.  In this environment, the core-dump
handler's attempt to pass the core-dump socket to a helper can be
intercepted; that allows said process to gain access to the file descriptor
from which the core dump can be read.  That, in turn, gives the attacker
the ability to read the (original, privileged) process's memory, happily
pillaging any secrets found there.  The example given by Qualys obtains the
contents of
/etc/shadow
, which is normally unreadable, but it
seems that SSH servers (and the keys in their memory) are vulnerable to the
same sort of attack.
Interested readers should consult the advisory for a much more detailed
(and coherent) description of how this attack works, as well as information
on some previous vulnerabilities in this area.  The key takeaways,
though, are that core-dump handlers on a number of widely used distributions
are vulnerable to this attack, and that reusable integer IDs as a way to
identify processes are just as much of a problem as the pidfd developers
have been saying over the years.
Toward a better API
The solution to this kind of race condition is to give the core-dump
handler a way to know that the process it is investigating is, indeed, the
one that crashed.  The 6.16 kernel contains two separate changes toward
that goal.  The first is
this patch from
Brauner
adding a new format specifier ("
%F
") for the string
written to
core_pattern
.  This specifier will cause the core-dump
handler to be launched with a pidfd identifying the crashed process
installed as file descriptor number three.  Since it is a pidfd, it will
always refer to the intended process and
44240909.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Linux内核在处理崩溃进程的核心转储（core dump）时存在的安全问题及改进措施。核心转储用于记录进程崩溃时的状态，但其处理机制长期以来导致了许多安全漏洞（CVEs）。当前的问题在于，核心转储处理程序作为用户模式助手，以完全特权运行，成为攻击目标。攻击者可以通过竞争条件漏洞，利用崩溃进程的PID替换，获取敏感信息如`/etc/shadow`文件内容。为解决此问题，6.16内核引入了改进措施，包括新增格式标识符`%F`，使处理程序能够通过pidfd准确识别崩溃的进程，从而减少此类漏洞。文章强调需要更安全的API来处理核心转储。

data.title: Last fifty years of integer linear programming: Recent practical advances (2024)
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了过去五十年混合整数线性规划（MILP）的进展，重点关注实际应用和近期计算性能的提升。MILP已成为运筹学的核心，现代求解器能高效解决十年前无法处理的问题，广泛应用于交通、物流、供应链、金融等领域。文章聚焦于分支定界法（branch-and-cut）、Dantzig-Wolfe分解和Benders分解三大方法，总结了关键研究成果，并指出MILP领域仍面临的挑战和未来研究方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：商业ILP求解器（如Gurobi）为何优于开源求解器，及其在实际应用中的表现和成本问题。

不同观点：
• [aquafox] 认为ILP问题由于其NP难性质，难以找到通用的高效解法，商业求解器通过大量针对特定子问题的启发式算法实现性能提升，而这些方法未进入公共领域。
• [dcminter] 通过自身经历说明算法和硬件的进步带来了巨大的性能提升，特别是在资源分配工具中，这种提升尤为明显，问题解决时间从长期运行缩短到几分钟。
• [tormeh] 提出实际应用中数值优化的实现可能因数据问题（如信任、数据质量）而失败，最终决策可能依赖于个人经验和直觉。
• [pradn] 引用研究数据，指出自1988年以来，LP求解器的速度提升了3300倍，结合硬件提升，整体性能提高了数百万倍，并提出在不同计算子领域中比较算法和硬件提升的必要性。
• [djoldman] 关注Gurobi的高昂价格，询问具体定价细节。
• [FabHK] 通过历史对比，说明自1990年代以来，求解LP问题的时间大幅缩短，现代MILP求解器的性能提升显著。
• [beret4breakfast] 认为目前基于ML/AI的方法在解决ILP等优化问题上效果不佳，实际应用中更高效的方法仍是运筹学（OR）方法，并分享了自己在调度优化中使用进化算法的经验。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了商业求解器Gurobi的高性能和昂贵价格，以及算法和硬件进步对求解速度的巨大影响。
• 实际应用中，数值优化的实现可能面临数据质量和信任问题，导致最终决策依赖于人工判断。
• 讨论中还涉及了ML/AI方法在ILP问题上的应用现状，目前看来这些方法尚不足以替代商业求解器。
• 历史对比和性能提升的数据为理解商业求解器的优势提供了量化支持。

Abstract
en
Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) has become a cornerstone of operations research. This is driven by the enhanced efficiency of modern solvers, which can today find globally optimal solutions within seconds for problems that were out of reach a decade ago. The versatility of these solvers allowed successful applications in many areas, such as transportation, logistics, supply chain management, revenue management, finance, telecommunications, and manufacturing. Despite the impressive success already obtained, many challenges remain, and MILP is still a very active field.
This article provides an overview of the most significant results achieved in advancing the MILP solution methods. Given the immense literature on this topic, we made deliberate choices to focus on computational aspects and recent practical performance improvements, emphasizing research that reports computational experiments. We organize our survey into three main parts, dedicated to branch-and-cut methods, Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition, and Benders decomposition. The paper concludes by highlighting ongoing challenges and future opportunities in MILP research.

data.title: Model Once, Represent Everywhere: UDA (Unified Data Architecture) at Netflix
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
Netflix的《Model Once, Represent Everywhere: UDA (Unified Data Architecture)》一文讨论了随着平台业务扩展带来的系统复杂性问题。不同系统对核心业务概念（如“演员”或“电影”）的建模不一致，导致重复、矛盾和数据质量问题。为了解决这些问题，Netflix开发了UDA（统一数据架构），旨在通过一次建模并在所有系统中复用，实现自动化、可发现性和语义互操作性。

UDA允许团队注册和连接域模型，编录和映射数据容器，自动生成各种系统的 schema，如GraphQL、Avro、SQL等，并实现数据在不同容器间的一致迁移。通过知识图谱和内部元模型Upper，UDA帮助开发者更轻松地查找、理解和利用业务概念和数据关系，减少手动工作并提高数据一致性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕统一数据定义（UDA）和数据模型在企业级应用中的挑战与优势的讨论。

不同观点：
• **jawns**：认为统一数据定义本质上是一个业务问题，而非技术问题。虽然避免了数据定义重复和偏差的问题，但任何微小的更改都需要跨部门批准，导致开发速度减慢。这种“红 tape”问题类似于大公司中更改按钮颜色需要两个月的经典问题。
• **Multicomp**：对统一数据方法的潜力持乐观态度，认为其有可能通过提供通用工具集和技能集来提高开发团队的效率，并期望这种方法能够解决大规模应用领域驱动设计（DDD）和语义概念的困难。
• **majormajor**：质疑这种方法是否真的能带来显著的业务改进，例如5%的收益或超过500万美元的改进。指出在统一数据表的尝试中，分析需求的不同可能导致独立分析的持续存在。
• **frankdejonge**：指出这里的“领域模型”主要是数据中心的，而领域建模应主要关注行为，而非底层数据结构。认为不同用例中对数据模型的不同表示是一种特性，而非问题。
• **cpard**：提到Uber的Dragon项目和相关的语义网工作，认为这些方法在语义的协议和维护上存在额外开销。并提出LLMs可能在今天帮助解决这一问题。
• **enjoylife**：怀疑这种内部工具的实际使用情况，认为日常工作中可能会出现许多绕过方案。
• **borromakot**：提到ASH（模型驱动开发）的长期实践经验，认为这是解决此类问题的途径。
• **bertylicious**：质疑这种方法与领域驱动设计（DDD）的关系，认为DDD中同一概念在不同系统中应有不同表示，而这似乎与UDA方法相矛盾。
• **bravesoul2**：对Netflix工程选择在Medium上发布文章感到不解，认为这样会因为弹窗问题流失读者。
• **heisenbit**：认为建立和维护一个通用的词汇表非常困难，尤其是在跨组织和时间的情况下。指出即使能生成系统间的接口，多层次的企业结构仍会带来复杂性。
• **Keyframe**：从多年处理相同问题的经验出发，认为UDA远不止是增强版的数据市场（Datamart++），其范围更广，并表示有兴趣进一步了解和实施。
• **twodave**：关注模型的版本管理和破坏性更改的处理，认为更分散的管理方式可以在小范围内进行更改。
• **oh_my_goodness**：认为这些活动本质上是软件开发，而非建模。对统一建模语言（UML）等方法持批评态度，认为过去尝试过类似的方法但效果不佳。
• **b0a04gl**：关心统一数据定义在运行时的实际执行情况，询问是否有机制能在下游系统违反语义假设时捕获问题，还是仅依赖信任机制。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于统一数据定义在业务和开发中的实际效果，以及其与领域驱动设计（DDD）的关系。
• 有人提出这种方法在大规模应用中的复杂性和维护难度，并讨论了LLMs在解决语义问题上的潜在应用。
• 实际使用情况和版本管理也是讨论中的重要问题。

As Netflix’s offerings grow — across films, series, games, live events, and ads — so does the complexity of the systems that support it. Core business concepts like ‘actor’ or ‘movie’ are modeled in many places: in our Enterprise GraphQL Gateway powering internal apps, in our asset management platform storing media assets, in our media computing platform that powers encoding pipelines, to name a few. Each system models these concepts differently and in isolation, with little coordination or shared understanding. While they often operate on the same concepts, these systems remain largely unaware of that fact, and of each other.
As a result, several challenges emerge:
Duplicated and Inconsistent Models
— Teams re-model the same business entities in different systems, leading to conflicting definitions that are hard to reconcile.
Inconsistent Terminology
— Even within a single system, teams may use different terms for the same concept, or the same term for different concepts, making collaboration harder.
Data Quality Issues
— Discrepancies and broken references are hard to detect across our many microservices. While identifiers and foreign keys exist, they are inconsistently modeled and poorly documented, requiring manual work from domain experts to find and fix any data issues.
Limited Connectivity
— Within systems, relationships between data are constrained by what each system supports. Across systems, they are effectively non-existent.
To address these challenges, we need new foundations that allow us to define a model once, at the conceptual level, and reuse those definitions everywhere. But it isn’t enough to just document concepts; we need to connect them to real systems and data. And more than just connect, we have to project those definitions outward, generating schemas and enforcing consistency across systems. The conceptual model must become part of the control plane.
These were the core ideas that led us to build UDA.
Introducing UDA
UDA (Unified Data Architecture)
is the foundation for connected data in
Content Engineering
. It enables teams to model domains once and represent them consistently across systems — powering automation, discoverability, and
semantic interoperability
.
Using UDA, users and systems can:
Register and connect domain models
— formal conceptualizations of federated business domains expressed as data.
Why?
So everyone uses the same official definitions for business concepts, which avoids confusion and stops different teams from rebuilding similar models in conflicting ways.
Catalog and map domain models to data containers
, such as GraphQL type resolvers served by a
Domain Graph Service
,
Data Mesh sources
, or Iceberg tables, through their representation as a graph.
Why?
To make it easy to find where the actual data for these business concepts lives (e.g., in which specific database, table, or service) and understand how it’s structured there.
Transpile domain models into schema definition languages
like GraphQL, Avro, SQL, RDF, and Java, while preserving semantics.
Why?
To automatically create consistent technical data structures (schemas) for various systems directly from the domain models, saving developers manual effort and reducing errors caused by out-of-sync definitions.
Move data faithfully between data containers
, such as from federated GraphQL entities to
Data Mesh
(a general purpose data movement and processing platform for moving data between Netflix systems at scale), Change Data Capture (CDC) sources to joinable Iceberg Data Products.
Why?
To save developer time by automatically handling how data is moved and correctly transformed between different systems. This means less manual work to configure data movement, ensuring data shows up consistently and accurately wherever it’s needed.
Discover and explore domain concepts
via search and graph traversal.
Why?
So anyone can more easily find the specific business information they’re looking for, understand how different concepts and data are related, and be confident they are accessing the correct information.
Programmatically introspect the knowledge graph
using Java, GraphQL, or SPARQL.
Why?
So developers can build smarter applications that leverage this connected business information, automate more complex data-dependent workflows, and help uncover new insights from the relationships in the data.
This post introduces the foundations of UDA
as a knowledge graph, connecting domain models to data containers through mappings, and grounded in an in-house
metamodel
, or model of models, called Upper. Upper defines the language for domain modeling in UDA and enables projections that automatically generate schemas and pipelines across systems.

Netflix的《Model Once, Represent Everywhere: UDA (Unified Data Architecture)》一文讨论了随着平台业务扩展带来的系统复杂性问题。不同系统对核心业务概念（如“演员”或“电影”）的建模不一致，导致重复、矛盾和数据质量问题。为了解决这些问题，Netflix开发了UDA（统一数据架构），旨在通过一次建模并在所有系统中复用，实现自动化、可发现性和语义互操作性。

UDA允许团队注册和连接域模型，编录和映射数据容器，自动生成各种系统的 schema，如GraphQL、Avro、SQL等，并实现数据在不同容器间的一致迁移。通过知识图谱和内部元模型Upper，UDA帮助开发者更轻松地查找、理解和利用业务概念和数据关系，减少手动工作并提高数据一致性。

data.title: The Many Sides of Erik Satie
data.author: anarbadalov
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了法国作曲家埃里克·萨蒂（Erik Satie）的多面性。他的《裸体舞》（Gymnopédies）和《玄秘曲》（Gnossiennes）广为人知，常出现在广告和电影配乐中，尽管这些作品创作于1887至1895年间，却有着超越时代的特质，既古老又现代。萨蒂不仅创作了这些迷人的钢琴小品，还涉足芭蕾舞剧、基督教寓言、戏剧以及电影配乐等多种形式。他融合了高雅文化与流行音乐， anticipates现代广告、耳机文化及个性化音乐的时代。萨蒂的个性矛盾，既是传统教会的成员，又活跃于低俗娱乐场所，对不同音乐形式兼收并蓄。他的情感生活同样复杂，最著名的是与艺术家苏珊娜·瓦拉东的短暂恋情。萨蒂是一个超越时代的创新者，其作品影响深远。

The Many Sides of Erik Satie
“The Satie life contains so much murk; his music sparkles with riverine clarity.”
By: Ian Penman
A↑
A↓
Off
Bright
Dark
Blues
Gray
BeeLine Reader
uses subtle color gradients to help you read more efficiently.
Contemplating
this book
, I asked a selection of young people: “Have you ever heard of Erik Satie?” Across the board, his name registered nothing. The moment I played the
Gnossiennes
and
Gymnopédies
however — “Oh, I LOVE those!” Everyone seems to know one or two, as if they’re now part of some collective audio memory. There are three
Gymnopédies
and six
Gnossiennes
, all composed between 1887 and 1895. Most people seem to know either “Gymnopédie #1” or “Gnossienne #1.” They are familiar props in TV adverts, film soundtracks, chill-out compilations. They are both just over three minutes — i.e., pop single length, not grand classical excursion.
This article is excerpted from Ian Penman’s book “
Erik Satie Three Piece Suite
” (Semiotext(e))
In the
Gymnopédies
, Roger Shattuck writes, Satie “takes one musical idea and … regards it briefly from three different directions.” “Gymnopédie #1” is probably Satie’s best-known piece. You reach for words like stately, unhurried, spacious, melancholy, poignant … but the music’s ineluctable strangeness remains. It is like a painting by Velázquez, where everything looks correct but the perspective seems somehow subtly awry. You’re pulled in without quite knowing why. Technically, there is no better description than this, from Constant Lambert: “Melodically speaking we find the juxtaposition of short lyrical phrases of great tenderness with ostinatos of extreme and deliberate bareness …. The strangeness of Satie’s harmonic colouring is due not to the chords themselves, but to the unexpected relationships he discovers between chords.”
“Gnossienne #1” radiates a mood of … what, exactly? Lightly anxious contemplation? Oddly contented melancholy? An icy but heartwarming breeze? For the three Gymnopédies, Satie specifies
sad and grave
in his instructions for pianists; but the mood is softer, gentler, more wistful. Slightly bruised, but not down and out. The
Gymnopédies
and
Gnossiennes
do not sound like 19th-century concert hall music; they sound like pieces composed by someone who knew there would one day be recording studios, CDs, downloads. They feel as old as sand, but strangely contemporary. To have even a wisp of your music eternally circling people’s minds like pollen in the air or a constellation in the night — this is not nothing. Who could have predicted that these brief, evanescent, weightless solo piano pieces would have such a prolonged afterlife? Satie is a crossover artiste, his catalogue ever reviving and never out of print.
A creature of his time, he anticipates a host of things we now take for granted — a world of adverts, headphones, leisure time, music as personal soundtrack.
If you only know these few exquisite morsels, you only know a tiny fraction of Satie. Until relatively recently, I didn’t know too much more myself. Dip a toe into the Satie rock pool and you soon discover a cove, a coastline, an entire horizon. As well as his solo-piano works, he wrote a riotous avant-pop ballet (
Parade
); a comical Christian allegory (
Uspud
); an intimate drama with samplings of Greek philosophy (
Socrate
); and his final work was a groundbreaking movie soundtrack (
Cinema
). A creature of his time, he anticipates a host of things we now take for granted — a world of adverts, headphones, leisure time, music as personal soundtrack.
In some ways, Satie feels like a long-ago ornament; at the same time, more playfully modern than our own increasingly doctrinaire era. This contradictory pulse —
on the one hand, on the other
— can be found in all aspects of his life. He is a one-man synthesis of Catholicism and Protestantism. He reconciles counterpoints of high culture and popular song. Founder of a church,
habitué
of low dives. His day job — or night apprenticeship — was in small clubs, memorizing the melodies of popular songs: things that made people dance and smile and sing. He is knowledgeable about ancient forms, but never wedded to how things have always been done. He loves both raucous cabaret songs and the sacred music of Palestrina. His work rings with marches, waltzes and hymns. He makes angular ballet from popular melodies; infuses classical forms with the ribald life of popular art.
He may have been an elective celibate or madly passionate — or both. There is his five-month-long
amour
with the artist Suzanne Valadon, shining like a sun over stony fields. Maybe he carries her memory deep inside for the rest of his life — a personal alchemical emblem, the lush rose on his barren cross. Such things do happen.
He could snub people for apparently trivial reasons — status and worth, we should always remember, are two completely different things — but he was generous with his time, especially when it came to young people. He could be pri

• **生活压力与认知衰退的关联**：squeegee_scream描述了由于生活压力、焦虑和抑郁导致的认知衰退经历，特别是成为父亲和丈夫后角色的转变带来的压力。这种衰退并非由生理疾病引起，而是由心理和生活压力造成。他通过药物、治疗和自我提升逐渐好转，但认知能力尚未完全恢复。

• **智力与自我价值的关系**：eszed和cjbgkagh认为，将自己的价值完全建立在智力上是一种误区。eszed分享了自己在认知能力严重下降时的体验，发现即使智力下降，依然能感受到爱、快乐和幽默。这表明自我价值不一定完全依赖于智力。

• **认知衰退的外部观察与应对**：GarnetFloride和at_a_remove从照顾认知衰退的亲人和自身经历出发，讨论了观察他人认知衰退的困难和痛苦。GarnetFloride提到照顾患有痴呆和中风的父母时，如何面对和补偿认知能力的下降。at_a_remove则分享了照顾患有认知衰退的朋友和观察母亲认知变化的经历。

• **生活压力与认知衰退的关联**：squeegee_scream描述了由于生活压力、焦虑和抑郁导致的认知衰退经历，特别是成为父亲和丈夫后角色的转变带来的压力。这种衰退并非由生理疾病引起，而是由心理和生活压力造成。他通过药物、治疗和自我提升逐渐好转，但认知能力尚未完全恢复。

• **智力与自我价值的关系**：eszed和cjbgkagh认为，将自己的价值完全建立在智力上是一种误区。eszed分享了自己在认知能力严重下降时的体验，发现即使智力下降，依然能感受到爱、快乐和幽默。这表明自我价值不一定完全依赖于智力。

• **认知衰退的外部观察与应对**：GarnetFloride和at_a_remove从照顾认知衰退的亲人和自身经历出发，讨论了观察他人认知衰退的困难和痛苦。GarnetFloride提到照顾患有痴呆和中风的父母时，如何面对和补偿认知能力的下降。at_a_remove则分享了照顾患有认知衰退的朋友和观察母亲认知变化的经历。

补充讨论：
• **对认知衰退的早期干预和治疗**：kevingadd提醒，暂时性的认知衰退可能是生活中需要立即处理的严重压力信号，忽视可能导致情况恶化。

• **特定术语和工具的讨论**：DougN7提到了“the genie”这一术语，可能指的是AI编码辅助工具，这与主要讨论点略有偏离，但表明了技术在认知功能中可能的辅助角色。

争议焦点：
• 争议并不明显，但不同用户对认知衰退的原因和应对方式有不同看法，比如有些人强调心理压力，而另一些人则关注生理健康问题。

data.title: Solar Orbiter gets world-first views of the Sun's poles
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary:
欧洲航天局（ESA）的太阳轨道器（Solar Orbiter）通过倾斜轨道，首次从黄道平面之外拍摄到太阳两极的图像。以往的太阳图像都来自太阳赤道区域，而太阳轨道器的新视角将帮助科学家更好地理解太阳的磁场、太阳活动周期及空间天气。2025年3月，太阳轨道器在距离太阳赤道17度的角度观测到南极，并计划未来进一步倾斜轨道以获得更佳视角。

太阳轨道器的科学仪器，包括偏振与日震成像仪（PHI）、极紫外成像仪（EUI）和日冕环境光谱成像仪（SPICE），提供了多角度的太阳观测数据。初步发现显示，太阳南极的磁场在太阳活动高峰期非常混乱，南北极磁场混合存在。这为了解太阳磁场翻转及11年活动周期提供了新线索。太阳轨道器的独特观测将开启太阳科学的新时代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类首次近距离观察太阳极区的意义及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [ahmedfromtunis] 认为，尽管人类对太阳的了解似乎很全面，但实际上非常有限，这次对太阳极区的观察提醒了我们这一点。他对科学探索工作表示支持和鼓励。
• [lostlogin] 对新闻中使用的“World First”表述提出质疑，认为“First Ever”可能更为合适。
• [superkuh] 指出，目前的观测只是稍微倾斜的角度，而非完全俯瞰极区。原本的计划是让探测器进入一个高倾角轨道，但因成本问题改为更便宜的方案，仅能提供接近黄道平面的观测。尽管如此，他认为这次任务仍然很酷。
• [sandworm101] 以幽默的方式表达了对未发现预期现象（如六边形结构）的失望，可能是因为一个旧赌约。
• [colordrops] 认为这次观测虽然看似微小，但实际上是人类历史上首次看到太阳极区，意义重大，令人惊叹。
• [wtcactus] 纠正其他评论者，指出1994-1995年Ulysses探测器已经进行过太阳极区探测，认为当前新闻报道中的声明不准确。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否真的是人类首次观测太阳极区。 [wtcactus] 提供了Ulysses探测器的例子，认为那才是首次。
• [superkuh] 提供了关于任务规划和预算削减的背景信息，指出原本有更雄心勃勃的计划，但因成本问题改为当前方案。
• 部分评论者如[ahmedfromtunis]和[colordrops]表达了对科学探索的积极态度和敬畏之情，而[lostlogin]和[sandworm101]则更多关注表述和幽默效果。
